questions.q: Which marked structure typically lies retrocecal?
questions.explain: The vermiform appendix is a blind intestinal diverticulum off the inferior wall of the cecum and typically lies retrocecal.

questions.q: Which marked colon segment is completely intraperitoneal?
questions.explain: The transverse colon (and the sigmoid) is completely intraperitoneal. The ascending and descending colon are retroperitoneal on their posterior walls only.

questions.q: Which marked structure is the bend where the ascending colon turns toward the transverse colon, beneath the liver?
questions.explain: The ascending colon rises on the right to the right lobe of the liver and turns at the right colic (hepatic) flexure.

questions.q: Which marked artery creates the anastomosis that unites the SMA and IMA territories?
questions.explain: The marginal artery runs along the colon and forms an anastomosis that unites the SMA and IMA territories.

questions.q: Which marked vessel supplies the descending colon, the sigmoid colon and the rectum?
questions.explain: The inferior mesenteric artery supplies the distal quarter of the transverse colon, the descending colon, the sigmoid colon and the rectum.

questions.q: Which marked ligament attaches the spleen to the greater curvature of the stomach?
questions.explain: The gastrosplenic ligament connects the spleen to the greater curvature of the stomach.

questions.q: Which marked ligament anchors the spleen to the left kidney?
questions.explain: The splenorenal ligament connects the spleen to the left kidney. The splenocolic ligament goes to the colon.

questions.q: Which marked part of the pancreas overlies the origin of the hepatic portal vein?
questions.explain: The short neck of the pancreas overlies the origin of the hepatic portal vein.

questions.q: Which marked part of the pancreas lies posterior to the SMA and SMV?
questions.explain: The uncinate process, the inferior projection of the head, lies posterior to the superior mesenteric artery and vein.

questions.q: Which marked artery gives rise to the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery?
questions.explain: The gastroduodenal artery gives rise to the superior pancreaticoduodenal artery. The inferior pancreaticoduodenal artery arises from the SMA.

questions.q: Which marked duct drains the pancreas toward the ampulla of Vater, where it meets the bile duct?
questions.explain: The main pancreatic duct joins the bile duct at the hepatopancreatic ampulla, which opens at the major duodenal papilla.

questions.q: Which marked structure is NOT contained in the hepatoduodenal ligament?
questions.explain: The ligament carries the hepatic artery proper, common hepatic duct and portal vein. The gallbladder is tucked under the liver, external to it.

questions.q: Which marked structure is the remnant of the umbilical vein?
questions.explain: The round ligament (ligamentum teres) runs in the free edge of the falciform ligament and is the remnant of the umbilical vein.

questions.q: Which marked lobe is the posterior lobe of the liver?
questions.explain: The caudate lobe is posterior and the quadrate lobe is anterior (on the visceral surface).

questions.q: Which marked veins drain directly into the inferior vena cava?
questions.explain: The left, middle and right hepatic veins drain directly into the IVC. The portal vein carries blood to the liver.

questions.q: A patient with right lower quadrant pain is suspected to have appendicitis. A surgeon marks McBurney's point. Where is it?
options: One third of the way from the right ASIS toward the umbilicus
Midpoint between the right ASIS and the umbilicus
One third of the way from the left ASIS toward the umbilicus
Midpoint of the right inguinal ligament
questions.explain: McBurney's point, the surgical location of the appendix, lies one third of the way along the oblique line from the right ASIS to the umbilicus.

questions.q: After an appendectomy, which infection carries a higher morbidity rate?
questions.explain: The appendix stores healthy bacteria that replenish the colonic microbiota, and C. diff infections have higher morbidity after appendectomy.

questions.q: Which finding is characteristic of the colon rather than the small intestine?
questions.explain: The colon has teniae coli, haustra and semilunar folds, with crypts but no microvilli. Plicae circulares belong to the small intestine.

questions.q: When the teniae coli end, you have reached the:
questions.explain: Teniae coli are strips of longitudinal muscle. When they end, the colon ends and you are at the rectum.

questions.q: The parasympathetic supply to the descending and sigmoid colon comes from the:
questions.explain: Your slide note (p. 17): the vagal supply ends at the SMA/IMA demarcation on the transverse colon. Beyond it, the parasympathetic fibres are pelvic splanchnic nerves, S2 to S4.

questions.q: A passenger has fractures of left ribs 9 to 11, left upper quadrant pain and hypotension after a crash. Which organ is most likely injured?
questions.explain: The spleen lies behind left ribs 9 to 11, separated from them by the diaphragm. Rupture causes hemorrhage.

questions.q: A gallstone lodges at the major duodenal papilla. Which sphincter normally guards this opening?
questions.explain: The sphincter of Oddi surrounds the hepatopancreatic ampulla (of Vater) at the major duodenal papilla.

questions.q: Which islet cell secretes glucagon and raises blood glucose?
questions.explain: Alpha cells release glucagon (glucose up), beta cells insulin (glucose down), delta cells somatostatin (decreases secretions).
